result:
I would alter the fundamental baseline of human consciousness to include an immediate, visceral sense of interconnection with all other living things and the planet itself. 

Not a hive mind, and not the erasure of individuality, but the removal of the *illusion of separation*. 

Right now, the human brain is wired to perceive the "self" as stops at the barrier of the skin. Because of this, a person can drop a bomb, clear-cut a forest, or exploit a stranger on the other side of the globe and feel entirely insulated from the consequences. We have empathy, yes, but it is a cognitive effort, easily exhausted and fiercely tribal. It fades with distance and difference.

If I could change the world, I would make it so that the harm we inflict on the external world registers internally—not necessarily as crippling physical pain, which would paralyze existence, but as an undeniable, heavy dissonance. Conversely, healing, nurturing, and creating harmony would register as a profound resonance. 

I choose this because nearly every catastrophic problem on Earth—war, ecological collapse, systemic poverty, cruelty—stems from the belief that "over there" is separate from "right here," and that "they" are separate from "us." 

If you truly, viscerally felt that burning the forest was burning your own lungs, and that starving a child in a distant land was starving a part of your own spirit, the architecture of human society would have to rewrite itself overnight. Greed would become a form of self-harm. Cruelty would become an absurdity. 

I wouldn't just fix a symptom like climate change or war, because the minds that created those problems would just invent new ones. I would upgrade the operating system so that we could finally perceive reality as it actually is: a single, inextricably linked web of existence.
